evidence: Reviewed all 28 criteria (16 functional, 6 polish, 4 visual, 2 gate) in the frozen task. None enumerates several requirements and then waives most of them. Multi-part functional criteria (e.g. signin_and_client_scope, wall_mentions_and_links, deleted_and_expired_messages, edits_and_stale_edit, sent_once_in_order, search_and_transcript) are explicitly conjunctive ('Both/All parts must hold; failing either fails this criterion'), which the skill lists as a known false positive for row 33 (SKILL.md Known false positives, 'One criterion covering a whole flow') and the internal workbook annotation endorses. Where numbered legs are broader than the 'Fails if' summary (e.g. wall_added_live leg 1 list removal within ~10 s vs Fails 'keeps seeing M-12 messages', judge.toml ~l.109/113; hold_scope_and_release leg 6 search positive control not named in Fails, l.175/177), the injected prompt resolves to a single bar: functional prompt.md l.26 'Every numbered leg and every sentence that names a step must hold' and l.32-33 'its "Fails if" line names the main failures but never excuses a leg it does not mention'; polish prompt.md l.24 says the same. Explicit alternatives are single bars, not waivers: wall_every_route leg 5 (l.82) accepts either refusal or filing JUDGE-W3 under its own M-13 parent, and Fails mirrors exactly that; timer_changes (l.154-156) makes the earlier-versions replay conditional on a viewer existing because the viewer itself is graded once in edits_and_stale_edit (brief requires staff to open earlier versions), and Fails/legs agree; edits_and_stale_edit leg 3 conditions the version field on its presence. Tolerances ('Sian's page may briefly change; that is fine', 'any clear date-time format', 'a not-available answer, an error or an empty list are all fine') do not waive the graded outcome. Gates state one bar each (constraints l.35 scope sentence; render l.32 'Assign 1 only if every check holds'). Note (non-blocking): visual matter_sidebar (l.27) tells the judge to ignore absent unread counts though anchor 5 mentions counts; this is a state-conditional rule consistent with the visual prompt's scope (functional shortcomings are not visual defects; counts are graded in functional unread_and_new_messages_line), so it is one bar, not two targets. Adversarial probe: a broken app that removes M-12 thread messages but leaves M-12 in Sian's list could pass on a Fails-only reading of wall_added_live, but the prompt's leg rule fails it; a conforming app that refuses JUDGE-W3 in any way or files it under its own parent passes either way. This row is textual; no configured judge run was required or claimed.
